## Flux 3 Max API

Flux 3 Max is a text to video and image to video model by Black Forest Labs, available on the Venice API as `flux-3-max-text-to-video`. It runs privately, with zero data retention.

Flux 3 Max is Black Forest Labs' post-trained Flux 3 video model, built for high visual quality at high speed. This text-to-video variant generates 5- to 20-second clips at up to 1080p with synchronized audio.

### Flux 3 Max API pricing

| Model ID | Variant | Privacy | Price |
|---|---|---|---|
| `flux-3-max-text-to-video` | Text to video | Private | from $0.1276 / sec |
| `flux-3-max-image-to-video` | Image to video | Private | from $0.1276 / sec |

Clip prices for `flux-3-max-text-to-video` with audio:

| Duration | 720p | 1080p |
|---|---|---|
| Per second | $0.1276 | $0.2175 |
| 5s | $0.64 | $1.09 |
| 10s | $1.28 | $2.17 |
| 20s | $2.55 | $4.35 |

Any length from 5 to 20 seconds, priced per second.

### Flux 3 Max specifications

| Spec | Value |
|---|---|
| Provider | Black Forest Labs |
| Released | Oct 16, 2026 |
| Privacy | Private |
| Status | Stable |
| Modes | text to video and image to video |
| Resolutions | 720p, 1080p |
| Durations | 5–20s, any whole second |
| Aspect ratios | auto, 21:9, 2:1, 16:9, 4:3, 1:1, 3:4, 9:16 |
| Audio | Always generated |

### How to use the Flux 3 Max API

Send requests to `POST https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/video/queue` with `"model": "flux-3-max-text-to-video"` and your API key.

```bash
# 1. Queue the job (returns a queue_id)
curl https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/video/queue \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VENICE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "model": "flux-3-max-text-to-video",
    "prompt": "Slow aerial drone shot over a misty mountain valley at golden hour",
    "duration": "5s",
    "resolution": "720p",
    "aspect_ratio": "auto"
  }'

# 2. Poll until the MP4 is ready
curl https://api.venice.ai/api/v1/video/retrieve \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $VENICE_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "model": "flux-3-max-text-to-video", "queue_id": "<queue_id>" }' --output video.mp4
```
